links.reason: Both set a rule for how the king takes revenue: Puram 184's elephant fed in balls (கவளங் கொளினே) against one loosed in the field, and Pazhamozhi 244's taking வருத்தாது, as if not taking, like the bee. The specific act matches and the teaches correctly notes Puram argues from the king's own ruin (தானும் உண்ணான்) while the ethics verse states it as a general rule.

Muthumozhikkanchi 26 is a single line whose sense the marker flags as uncertain (முறையில் அரசர்நாட் டிருந்து பழியார் may mean they are not blamed for staying, not that they keep silent). The teaches builds a causal story, silence because there is no recourse, that neither line states; Pazhamozhi 247 says only that subjects can do nothing (செய்வதென்).

Pazhamozhi 297 sets the enemy who is far off (வேறிடத்தார்), even a flood of them, against the deceitful friendship close by (சார்ந்த கழிநட்பு), the debt eaten in one's own house; this explains Kural 882's preference of fearing கேள்போல் பகைவர். The ranking by nearness is in the Tamil; calling வெள்ளம் a natural force is a little loose, since it may mean a multitude.

The consolation reading of 'உண்ணும் துணைக்காக்கும் கூற்று' is not secure: under the heading நட்பில் விலக்கு the proverb more naturally likens the plotting friend to Death that guards its prey until the time to eat, a warning, not fate as shelter. Naladiyar 110's fixed term (சிறுகாலைப் பட்ட பொறி) is not named in Pazhamozhi 135, so the link stretches the proverb.

The shared figure of Death as eater is real (கூற்றமுங் கூறுவ செய்துண்ணாது; உண்ணும் துணைக்காக்கும் கூற்று). But the teaches depends on the contested consolation reading of Pazhamozhi 135, where the proverb may instead liken the treacherous friend to Death biding its time.

Manimekalai's மெய்யுணர்வு இன்றி மெய்ப் பொருள் உணர்வு அரிய takes up Kural 354's contrast of ஐயுணர்வு and மெய்யுணர்வு and turns it on the materialist. That is an application of the couplet, not a limit or condition on it, so qualifies is the wrong type.

The milk-white one and the snake-bannered one plainly point to the epic pair by epithet, and the verse scorns மாதவம் done instead of joining the battle as help after the festival (கழிவிழாத் தோளேற்று). Set against Kural 788's ஆங்கே, the pairing makes timing the test of a friend's help.

links.reason: Kural 699 forbids presuming on favour (கொளப்பட்டேம் என்றெண்ணி); Pazhamozhi 283 adds the case of the king's forbearance shown with displeasure (பொறாஅன் போலப் பொறுத்தால்) and the repeated offence, the boil on the hump. The second false ground for presuming is a real development.

241 demands that a king punish even his own (தங்கண்ணர் ஆயினும் ... ஒறுக்க), 256 praises those slow to anger (ஒல்லை வெகுளார்) at harm done to them (இன்னாசெய் தாரையும்). The pair genuinely separates punishing wrong from quick anger at personal injury, a fair qualification.

Both meet on the specific act of how a gift is given: Puram 159 refuses a killer elephant given grudgingly (தவிர்ந்துவிடு பரிசில் கொள்ளலென்) and takes a kunri given gladly (உவந்து), and Kural 1057 names the asker's joy at giving without scorn (இகழ்ந்தெள்ளாது). The teaches correctly says the Puram turns this into the bard's rule for accepting at all.

The two kinds of trust differ: Kural 506 is about trusting the kinless (அற்றாரைத் தேறுதல்) for service, Pazhamozhi 177 about trusting kin or friend with one's weak point (அற்றத்தால் தேறார்). The necessary-but-not-sufficient framing is fair, but the list_adds' 'self-interest outruns every bond' rests on சீர்ந்தது, whose sense the marker admits is uncertain.

Kar Narpathu 7 does not offer his aim of giving and crushing (ஈதலும் ... தெறுதலும்) as the guarantee of return; it is the rain (மழை ... தரூஉம்) that will bring him. The 'grievance' in Kural 1263 comes from the commentator's reading of துணை, so the teaches' contrast overstates both verses, and qualifies does not describe the relation.

303 says nothing is stronger than numbers (பன்மையிற் பாடுடைய தில்); 307 says division is in everyone (வேற்றுமை யார்க்குமுண்டு), so the able man kills the hundred. The second limits the first: numbers count only while undivided, a true qualification within one book.

Kural 883 says to fear the உட்பகை at home; Pazhamozhi 308 says to win the enmity living inside the enemy (தம்பகைக் குள்வாழ் பகை). The teaches' point, that the same inner enmity is danger or weapon by whose house it is in, is specific, and the like-cures-like proverbs (கள்ளினால் கள்ளறுத்தல், முள்ளினால் முட்களைதல்) are rightly named as what the couplet lacks.

Kural 90 makes the guest the fragile party (முகந்திரிந்து நோக்கக் குழையும்); Pazhamozhi 337 lays a duty on the great guest not to strain the poor host (நல்கூர்ந்தவர்க்கு ... செல்விருந்தாகிச் செலவேண்டா). That is a real limit on hospitality from the guest's side, and the sparrow proverb counts the host's cost.

300's வன்பாட்டவர் and புன்பாட்டவர் are one scale, strong and petty, so the teaches' split between strength and standing is read into பாடு. On the plain reading 302 (press the weak, மெலியாரை மீதூரும்) and 300 (no gain in fighting the petty) pull against each other, and 302 itself may be ironic.

136 says the cherished reserve friend fails (உற்றுழி ஒன்றுக்கு உதவலர்); 341 says even a crab saved a man (நண்டேயும்). The contrast is real but neither verse limits the other, so qualifies is a poor fit and the lesson is thin.

Naladiyar 189 keeps the pure unshaken by slander (துளக்க மிலாதவர்); Pazhamozhi 77 has the worthy refuse to join such talk and turn away (சொல்லோ டொருப்படார் ... மாறுப). The pairing of inner steadiness with outer withdrawal is specific, and the slanderer's pose as protector (காப்பாரே போன்று) is in the verse.

links.reason: Both refuse unjust gain, and the proverb (தீயன ஆவதே போன்று கெடும்) does deny that the gain is real. But the teaches needs a strong reading of the Kural's concessive நன்றே தரினும, as if the couplet grants the gain truly brings good, and the wave in the address is ornament the list_adds leans on.

Kural 850 leaves blank what is denied (உண்டென்பது இல்லென்பான்); Pazhamozhi 108 names a denial, மறுமையொன் றுண்டோ, and judges it by the bad exchange of the ghee cake for brick. The teaches openly says the pairing supplies the content, which is a fair application.

Both use சால்பு: Pazhamozhi 59 lets it come to one who endures (தானோன்றிட வரும் சால்பு) and finds no gain in punishing, while Kural 987 asks that the wrongdoer be done good (இனியவே செய்யாக்கால்). Setting the two thresholds side by side is specific and correct.

Both state that people come for what can be had: no one seeks frogs after digging a tank (குளந்தொட்டுத் தேரை வழிச்சென்றார் இல்), and the poor have no kin (இலாஅர்க் கில்லை தமர்). The two-sides reading is good, but calling Pazhamozhi's statement a comfort overstates a verse that states the law without praise.

230's elephant that went (மேற்சென்றது) to the Karuvur man is good fortune only by the tradition of the elephant choosing a king; the verse does not say so, and விழுமிய may also carry the sense of affliction (விழுமம்). The teaches' claim that உறற்பால covers good lot rests on that traditional identification.

Both rank the poverty of the worthy above others' wealth with an image of what is drunk or eaten: the small well beside the sea (அறுநீர்ச் சிறுகிணறு) and old ghee beside buttermilk (மோரின் முதுநெய்). The teaches rightly separates use from kind, and the list_adds correctly notes the comparison is with the small (சிறியவர்), not those who do not know the next world (மறுமை யறியாதார்).

Kural 772 measures valour by its target (யானை பிழைத்தவேல்); Pazhamozhi 319 names the opposite type, silent before the able (காத்தாற்று நிற்பாரைக் கண்டால் எதிருரையார்) and riding over the helpless, the razor sharpened for a leaf. The same claim, with the bully's two faces added.

Both reason from youth's passing (கனியுதிர்ந்து வீழ்ந்தற் றிளமை; இளமையும் தருவதோ இறந்த பின்னே), but to different audiences in different situations: the moralist warns men off desire, the friend keeps a husband from leaving. The teaches itself calls them 'opposite lives', which is different counsel for different cases rather than incompatible claims about the same case.

Lines 1-2 of Pazhamozhi 226 fault recipients who would not help in turn when need comes (உற்றால் ஒன்று ஆற்றி நிகராகி ... அல்லர்), which comes close to expecting a return. So the teaches' 'no repayment, but gladness' and the list_adds' 'without retracting its rule against seeking return' are not secure against Naladiyar 98's மாறீவார்க் கீதல் பொலிகடன்.

Both say ill-gotten wealth perishes: அழக் கொண்ட எல்லாம் அழப்போம் and தீயன ஆவதே போன்று கெடும். The teaches ('self-cancelling twice over') restates that shared claim in grander words; the list_adds' point that the good refuse to want it (நயப்பவோ) is true but small.

There is a defensible tension: Naladiyar 195 says good and bad குலம் are words only (சொல்லள வல்லால் பொருளில்லை), while Pazhamozhi 147 says one's own சாதி shows through concealment (மறைப்பினும் ... மிக்கு விடும்). But the note does not say which reading it depends on, the episode is obscure (காப்பான் twice, மேய்ப்பாட்டது), and the quatrain denies the worth of birth rank, not that birth leaves traits, so the list_adds overstates.

Both make a fort (அரண்) useless without an inner quality. But the note narrows Kural 750's வினைமாட்சி to courage, while the couplet means excellence in action generally. The Pazhamozhi's reading of வன்சார்பு against தஞ்சார்பு is also flagged uncertain.

Acharakkovai 39's தமக்கென்று உலையேற்றார் carries Kural 229's தாமே தமியர் உணல் back to the hearth. The link describes the rule as the text's order of the house, with its எச்சில் and மனைப்பலி provisions, and does not urge it as advice.

Kural 657 ranks the poverty of the worthy above wealth got under blame (பழிமலைந்து எய்திய); Pazhamozhi 89 ranks it above wealth that the small hold (சிறியவர் எய்திய செல்வம்). The teaches' two grounds, how the wealth was got and who holds it, is exact and specific.

222 depicts a show of help followed by dashed hope (நற்செய்கை செய்வார்போல் காட்டி நசையழுங்க); 225 says refusal is no fault (இல்லென் பதூஉம் வசையன்று) but killing hope costs the next world (நசைகொன்றான் செல்லுலகம் இல்). The second names the price of what the first shows.

Both name five dependants. Acharakkovai 21 turns Kural 43's ஐம்புலத்தாறு into an order at the meal (இவர்க்கூண் தொடுத்தல்லால் உண்ணார்), with the cow and the caged creatures (பசு, சிறை) in the list and the self left out. The teaches is true, though gods and ancestors also drop away.

Both use the honoured dog: Naladiyar 345's dog fed from gold still eyes leftovers, while Pazhamozhi 105's நாய்மேல் தவிசிடுதல் blames whoever gives the great man's honour to the small. The shift of blame from the honoured to the honourer is real and specific.

The two images are different, a beauty growing old alone (தமியள்மூத் தற்று) and the eye lost with its beauty (அழகொடு கண்ணின் இழவு), so there is no shared distinctive image. What they share is the claim that the non-giver's wealth is waste, so agrees fits better.

Kural 796 makes ruin the rod that measures kin (நீட்டி அளப்பதோர் கோல்); Pazhamozhi 134 reports what that measure finds: the thousand who ate at the house, and no friends for the ruined in the Kali age (கெட்டார்க்கு நட்டாரோ இல்). The couplet's consolation turned into a bleak verdict is a true development.

Kural 451 says greatness fears the small company (சிற்றினம் அஞ்சும்) without saying what it fears. Pazhamozhi 113's worms bound into the wound (புழுப்பெய்து புண்பொதியும்) gives the mechanism: harm fostered by one's own care (பேணி, ஒழுக்கி).

Pazhamozhi 195 does join private scrutiny (நாடுக தான்கண்ட நுட்பத்தை) with conformity (ஓடுக ஊரோடு), which bears on Kural 426. But the verse lists its counsels and does not rank them, and line 2 (நீத்தார் நெறியொரீ) is uncertain, so the list_adds' 'only then conforming' reads in an order of priority.

Kural 693 says suspicion, once roused, cannot be cleared (கடுத்தபின் தேற்றுதல் யார்க்கும் அரிது); Pazhamozhi 335 carries this to entering a friend's house alone, where the town's talk leaves no witness (கரியோ இல்லை), as no dam holds a flood. Avoiding the occasion is the shared rule, carried into the town.

Item 1, நகை, is the act shared with Kural 694's சேர்ந்த நகை, so the item carries the link. Acharakkovai 73 sets it with yawning, hawking and sneezing before the great (பெரியார்முன்), and the link presents this as a rule the text states. The 'misread sign' reason for the Kural is a commentator's, but it is fair.

Naladiyar 141 allows the rags (உடுக்கை உலறி) and keeps the principle (கொள்கையில் குன்றார்); Pazhamozhi 329 insists on outward show (புறத்தால் பொலிவுறல் வேண்டும்) because the clothed are not asked whether they have eaten. Splitting inner principle from outward appearance is a real and specific qualification.

verses.note: A sequence of morning household rites with no count word, so no items are given.
Places to avoid (gaming hall, noisy arena) are prudence rather than bodily or ritual purity, so the domain is all and no norm is given.
Line 1 states a gender norm (நாணின்றி ஆகாது பெண்மை) inside a general maxim.
It lists the days on which பார்ப்பார் do not recite but has no count word, so no items are given; the norm is caste because the rule names பார்ப்பார்.
Conduct before the lord; no count word, so no items are given.
The wife's role in hosting guests is praised rather than laid down as a rule, so no gender norm is given.
பெரிய குடிப்பிறத்தார் names lineage, but the verse states no birth rule, so no norm is given.
